messages.subject: Davis R Users' Group schedule for Winter 2024
messages.subject_clean: Davis R Users' Group schedule for Winter 2024
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

For winter 2024, the Davis R Users Group will have a new meeting time: 10-12 in the Datalab Classroom (360 Shields Library). Our first meeting of the quarter is TOMORROW, which will be a group work-session where you can come to work, get help with your R code, or just chat about R. As always, the meting will be hybrid in-person and remote over Zoom at https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862

This quarter's schedule will feature fewer mini-workshops and more chances to ask our expeRts for help with your code and analyses.

Another way to get help with your R questions is to post your question any time to our Discourse Q+A forum at https://d-rug.discourse.group

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators
________________________________________________________________
Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

--
Check out our R resources at https://d-rug.github.io/
And please post questions/comments at https://d-rug.discourse.group/

messages.subject: Free R workshops start next week!
messages.subject_clean: Free R workshops start next week!
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!
The UC Davis Datalab is offering a series of free R workshops this quarter. Next week begins our "Intermediate R" workshop series, with sessions on R Scripting on Tuesday January 30  and R Debugging on Thursday February 1, respectively. Both sessions are 10am-noon in the DataLab Classroom (360 Shields Library). There is a virtual attendance option over Zoom, as well.

The Intermediate R workshops will continue in March, with Data Cleaning on Tuesday March 5 and Data Reshaping on Thursday March 7.

The workshops are free but registration is required. Registration links are below:

- Writing Scripts In R. January 31 (Tuesday) 10am-noon. Register here: https://reservations.library.ucdavis.edu/event/11931823
- Debugging In R. February 1 (Thursday) 10am-noon. Register here: https://reservations.library.ucdavis.edu/event/11931826
- Cleaning Data In R. March 5(Tuesday) 10am-noon. Register here: https://reservations.library.ucdavis.edu/event/11931814
- Reshaping Data in R. March 7(Thursday) 10am-noon. Register here: https://reservations.library.ucdavis.edu/event/11931814

Thanks ,and we hope to see you there!
-Wes

messages.body_plain:
Just a heads up that #maptimeDavis has an R topic this week. Tomorrow 10:00-12:00 in the Physical Sciences & Engineering Library’s Seminar Room. All are welcome! More details below.

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Specialist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

Pronouns: she, her, hers

From: Michele M Tobias
Sent: Wednesday, January 24, 2024 11:01 AM
To: geospatial Sympa List <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: FW: #maptimeDavis Workshop: Downloading Satellite Data from Spatiotemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC) using R

Just a quick reminder that this Friday from 10:00-12:00 #maptimeDavis is having a STAC workshop! Learn about using an API to get Landsat satellite data from NASA’s online STAC catalog. More details & registration info forwarded below.

To follow along, you’ll need the following – all of these are free of charge:
A recent version of R (4.1 or newer) and R studio
A NASA EarthData Login account:  https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/eosdis/science-system-description/eosdis-components/earthdata-login

And remember that’s we’ve moved for this quarter! Don’t come to DataLab. We’re in the Seminar Room (room 1025) in the UC Davis PSEL (Physical Sciences & Engineering Library). Zoom details will be emailed upon registration for people wishing to attend online.

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Specialist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

Pronouns: she, her, hers

From: geospatial Sympa List (request) <geospatia...@lists.ucdavis.edu> On Behalf Of Matthew Conner
Sent: Monday, January 22, 2024 12:44 PM
To: geospatial Sympa List <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: [geospatial] #maptimeDavis Workshop: Downloading Satellite Data from Spatiotemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC) using R

#maptimeDavis: Downloading Satellite Data from Spatiotemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC) using R
January 26 @ 10:00 am - 12:00 pm

Learn how to connect to, search, and download data from a STAC in R.

Please RSVP via our  Registration Link <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScOnzUEyuZDYOzYJFvoHTr13Xo9qUSqFu5pSBEExoBJnTFcew/viewform?usp=sf_link>

Description

Spatiotemporal asset catalogs (STAC) are growing in popularity as a way to make data available in a standardized way, but getting started with these tools is not always straight forward or clear to people who did not set them up. In this workshop, we hope to demystify working with STAC catalogs. Learn how to connect to, search, and download data from a STAC in R.

By the end of the workshop, participants will be familiar with STAC terminology, be able to connect to a STAC, and search and downlaod STAC data.

Concepts Covered:  STAC Catalogs, APIs, Aerial and Satellite Photography, Remote Sensing, NDVI, NDWI, R, Programming

Speakers: Michele Tobias (UCD DataLab) & Alex Mandel (Development Seed)

Michele Tobias is a geospatial data scientist with a background in geospatial methods for ecology. Michele earned her PhD from UC Davis in Geography where she studied California’s sandy beach ecosystem with traditional phytosociological methods and innovative remote sensing tools and was a postdoc at the UC Davis Information Center for the Environment. In her current position as a geospatial data scientist at UC Davis DataLab, she applies geospatial tools to new avenues of research across disciplines.

Alex Mandel is a geospatial engineer with an emphasis in open source solutions. He currently works at Development Seed, interfacing between scientists and data providers working with earth observation data, helping ensure access to data as a key component of solving problems with open science. Alex has a PhD from UC Davis in Geography, and is a participant in the STAC and OSGeo communities.

Location: Seminar Room (room 1025) in the UC Davis PSEL (Physical Sciences & Engineering Library). Zoom details will be emailed upon registration for people wishing to attend online.

Prerequisites:  The instructors will assume participants have an introductory understanding of programming, in particular with R, and that they have an introductory understanding of spatial data formats, in particular vector and raster data.

Software: Please download and install R and RStudio before the workshop.

Whenever possible, #maptimeDavis Workshops will be recorded and posted on the  DataLab YouTube channel <https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTooXK1RiSHNbWsmeqz0W6g>. #maptimeDavis Studio will not be recorded to encourage open discussion. Weekly reminders will be sent on the Geospatial Email List <https://lists.ucdavis.edu/sympa/info/geospatial>.

#maptimeDavis Workshops and Studio are a product of UC Davis DataLab’s Spatial Sciences Research Cluster <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/spatial-sciences/> and are supported by the contributions and participation of our community. Please send questions to Michele Tobias mmto...@ucdavis.edu

Matt Conner

Student Services Department

Library

University of California, Davis

on behalf of the #maptimeDavis council
